claims.statement: UNECE Global Technical Regulation No. 22 establishes an international framework for in-vehicle battery durability for electrified vehicles, confirming that battery durability and state tracking are standardisable technical concerns.

The EU battery-passport regime includes battery-specific use information and differentiated records, which can improve future access to provenance but does not by itself guarantee an independent used-vehicle condition assessment.

Hypothesis: dealers, leasing fleets, buyers, and warranty providers will pay for a neutral certificate when battery uncertainty materially affects a used EV transaction; conversion and predictive validity require live testing.

contrary_evidence: Vehicle manufacturers increasingly expose state-of-health information, so a certificate that merely repeats dashboard data is not defensible.
Battery passports may improve provenance over time, potentially reducing information asymmetry for newer vehicles.

economics.acquisition_route: Pilot with independent EV inspectors, dealer batch days, lease-return partnerships, and a verifiable certificate displayed in listings
economics.founder_net_worth_path: Hypothesis: a network completing 30,000 tests annually at 120 PLN platform contribution plus 150 partners and data contracts could generate 4-6m PLN revenue; majority ownership of the certification network could exceed 5m PLN founder equity in five to eight years
economics.founder_time: Up to 15-20 hours weekly during protocol pilots; field inspections must migrate to trained partners for scale
economics.gross_margin_basis: Founder-delivered inspections are labour-bound at roughly 40-60% gross margin; licensed partner tests and data APIs could exceed 80%
economics.payback: One avoided mispriced battery or reduced warranty dispute can repay many tests; partner acquisition should repay within 50-100 inspections
economics.pricing: Hypothesis: 400-900 PLN retail inspection, 150-350 PLN fleet or dealer volume price, plus 500-2,000 PLN monthly partner software and data fees
economics.retention_or_repeat: Dealers and fleets test recurring inventory, while later follow-up readings strengthen the model and warranty value

fingerprint.compounding_advantage: A trusted certificate brand and longitudinal model-level dataset linking test signals to price, warranty, and degradation outcomes
fingerprint.customer: Used-EV dealers, leasing fleets, independent inspection stations, warranty providers, and buyers
fingerprint.distribution_mechanism: Dealer and inspection-station integrations, lease-return workflows, used-car marketplace badges, and warranty partnerships
fingerprint.offer_and_business_model: Model-aware battery-health test, uncertainty-rated certificate, partner QA software, and residual-risk data API
fingerprint.payer_and_paid_event: Dealer, fleet, buyer, or warranty partner pays per signed inspection; inspection networks pay software and protocol licence fees
fingerprint.problem_trigger: An EV is appraised, returned from lease, listed for sale, financed, warranted, or disputed

founder_fit: Strong quantitative, longevity-of-assets, and battery-adjacent fit with a Warsaw test market. The founder can develop uncertainty-aware models and partner tooling without being camera-facing. Qualified EV technicians, legal review, and insurer input are required before guarantees.
risks: An overconfident certificate can create financial and safety liability.
Manufacturer software changes or locked diagnostics may break coverage.
A field-service model can become labour-heavy unless protocol, training, and partner quality scale cleanly.

structure.commercial_archetype: Certification protocol, licensed inspection network, and residual-risk data asset
structure.control_point: The trusted battery condition certificate used at the transaction or warranty decision
structure.critical_dependency: Predictively valid model coverage and dealer, insurer, or marketplace acceptance of the certificate

thesis: Create a repeatable, signed battery-health inspection for used EV transactions, beginning as a mobile Warsaw service and expanding through licensed inspection partners. Combine vehicle-reported state, controlled charge or drive observations, model-specific uncertainty, and tamper-evident provenance. The defensible asset is the trusted certificate plus the longitudinal link between test features, resale value, warranty events, and later degradation.
title: Used-EV Battery Trust Certificate Network
uncertainties: Which vehicle models expose sufficiently reliable diagnostic data without prohibited access or warranty issues.
Whether a short inspection predicts future degradation and transaction value well enough to insure or warrant.
Whether the payer is the buyer, dealer, leasing company, inspection chain, or warranty provider.
